paras: 美國8月貿易逆差擴大至1,056億美元，創2025年初以來最大，且超出市場預期。AI建設帶動半導體與設備進口，加上能源成本上升及關稅政策干擾，推升進口額至歷史新高，貿易恐再度拖累第三季經濟成長。不過，強勁內需也顯示消費與企業投資仍具支撐力。
美國商務部周二(6日)公布，8月商品與服務貿易逆差較前月擴大13.7%，高於市場預估的約1,020億美元，7月逆差則修正為928億美元。8月進口月增4.3%至4,208億美元，出口僅增1.4%至3,152億美元，成長速度明顯落後。

AI建設拉動進口 半導體增額創紀錄

8月商品進口月增5.3%至3,422億美元，商品出口增加2.2%至2,057億美元。經通膨調整後，商品貿易逆差擴大至1,147億美元，為2025年3月以來最大。
包含電腦及周邊、半導體與電信設備的資本財進口，較前月增加62億美元。其中，半導體進口增加24億美元，創單月增額紀錄，民用飛機與電信設備進口也上升，反映AI投資熱潮持續仰賴海外供應。
包含石油及石油產品的工業原料進口增加91億美元，出口增加63億美元，其中原油出口增加20億美元。非貨幣性黃金進出口也同步增加。相較之下，服務出口大致持平，受訪美旅客支出降至2023年8月以來最低拖累。
美國第二季內需增速創逾三年半最快，消費與AI相關設備投資強勁。8月消費支出及核心資本財訂單、出貨數據顯示，這股動能延續至第三季，企業則持續依靠進口滿足需求。

貿易恐續拖累GDP 關稅未阻進口攀升

貿易已連續三季拖累美國國內生產毛額(GDP)，經濟學家估計，第三季拖累幅度可能達2.5個百分點。最新數據公布前，亞特蘭大聯準銀行GDPNow模型估計，淨出口將拉低第三季GDP成長率2.59個百分點，將是2025年初以來最大拖累。
不過，市場對第三季經濟成長率的預估多高於年率3%，預期消費支出可抵銷進口帶來的拖累，優於第二季的2.2%。
川普主張加徵關稅有助縮小逆差，但進口仍持續攀升。關稅變動、戰爭引發的油價波動及供應鏈挑戰，也使未經通膨調整的每月貿易數據劇烈起伏。
分國別來看，美國對加拿大商品逆差擴大至2025年初以來最高。8月貿易談判破局後，兩國企業搶在關稅生效前加速出貨；美國8月22日起對數十億美元加拿大商品課徵50%關稅，加拿大隨後反制。美國對墨西哥、越南的商品逆差均小幅擴大至新高，對半導體重要供應地台灣的逆差也增加。
paras_en: U.S. August trade deficit widened to $105.6 billion, the biggest since early 2025 and above market expectations. AI build‑out drove semiconductor and equipment imports, while higher energy costs and tariff policy disruptions pushed total imports to a historic high, threatening to again drag down third‑quarter economic growth. Nevertheless, strong domestic demand shows consumption and corporate investment remain supportive.

The U.S. Department of Commerce reported on Tuesday (the 6th) that the goods‑and‑services trade deficit for August expanded 13.7% from the prior month, exceeding the market forecast of roughly $102 billion; the July deficit was revised to $92.8 billion. August imports rose 4.3% month‑over‑month to $420.8 billion, while exports increased only 1.4% to $315.2 billion, a clearly slower growth rate.

AI construction pulled imports higher, with semiconductor imports hitting a record increase. August goods imports rose 5.3% month‑over‑month to $342.2 billion, while goods exports grew 2.2% to $205.7 billion. After inflation adjustment, the goods trade deficit expanded to $114.7 billion, the largest since March 2025.

Imports of capital goods—including computers and peripherals, semiconductors and telecom equipment—rose by $6.2 billion from the prior month. Semiconductor imports alone jumped $2.4 billion, setting a new single‑month increase record, while civil aircraft and telecom equipment imports also rose, reflecting the continued reliance on overseas supply for the AI investment boom.

Imports of industrial raw materials, including oil and petroleum products, increased by $9.1 billion, while exports rose $6.3 billion, with crude oil exports up $2.0 billion. Non‑monetary gold imports and exports also grew. By contrast, services exports were roughly flat, weighed down by U.S. visitor spending falling to its lowest level since August 2023.

U.S. domestic demand in the second quarter grew at the fastest pace in more than three and a half years, with strong consumer spending and AI‑related equipment investment. August consumer outlays and core capital‑goods orders and shipments indicate this momentum will carry into the third quarter, as firms continue to rely on imports to meet demand.

Trade has been a drag on U.S. gross domestic product (GDP) for three consecutive quarters, and economists estimate the third‑quarter drag could reach 2.5 percentage points. Ahead of the latest data release, the Atlanta Fed’s GDPNow model projected that net exports would shave 2.59 percentage points off third‑quarter GDP growth, the biggest drag since early 2025.

However, market forecasts for third‑quarter GDP growth are generally above an annualized 3%, with expectations that consumer spending will offset the import‑related drag, improving on the second quarter’s 2.2% rate.

Former President Trump argues that higher tariffs help narrow the deficit, yet imports keep climbing. Tariff changes, war‑driven oil‑price volatility and supply‑chain challenges also cause unadjusted monthly trade figures to swing sharply.

By country, the U.S. deficit with Canada rose to its highest level since early 2025. After trade talks broke down in August, firms in both nations rushed to ship goods before tariffs took effect; the U.S. imposed a 50% tariff on billions of dollars of Canadian goods starting August 22, prompting a Canadian retaliation. Deficits with Mexico and Vietnam also edged higher to new highs, and the deficit with Taiwan, a key semiconductor supplier, increased as well.

items.title_en: Taiwan Dollar Trading Forces Stuck in Tug‑of‑War, Closes at 31.781 per USD, Up 0.7 cents
paras: 台股加權指數上看5萬點近關情怯，台北匯市也陷入震盪，新台幣由升轉貶，但收盤前15分鐘又轉升，買賣匯力道陷入拉鋸戰，新台幣兌一美元終場收在31.781元，升值0.7分，台北外匯經紀公司成交值縮至16.04億美元。
新台幣今日以31.76元、升值2.8分開出後，最高見到31.699元，午盤過後轉貶，最低至31.823元，全日高低價差1.24角。
觀察主要亞幣，韓元升值近0.3%，泰銖升約0.1%，星元升0.05%左右，新台幣收升0.02%，日元轉貶近0.2%，而美元指數跌跌近0.2%。
元大投顧指出，由於美債殖利率居高不下、美伊地緣政治詭譎多變、美國期中選舉等因素，恐使國際股市波動加劇，建議投資人在市場上須留意強勢股追價風險。
統一投顧則提到，儘管國際油價和美債殖利率居高不下，但輝達市值創高，市場將焦點轉向科技財報，台股目前技術面強勢，台指期夜盤再衝5萬大關展現多方控盤底氣，本周上市櫃公司陸續公布9月營收，AI 供應鏈族群預期可望持續繳出佳績，同時，世界AI高峰會和大立光(3008-TW)、台積電(2330-TW)等法說會即將登場，台股題材充沛。
paras_en: The Taiwan Stock Exchange weighted index hovered near the 50,000‑point psychological barrier, and the Taipei foreign‑exchange market also entered a range‑bound session. The New Taiwan dollar (NTD) switched from appreciation to depreciation, but turned back up in the last 15 minutes of trading, leaving the buying‑selling pressure in a tug‑of‑war. The NTD finished at 31.781 per US dollar, up 0.7 cents, while the turnover of Taipei FX brokerage firms fell to $1.604 billion.
The NTD opened today at 31.76, up 2.8 cents, rose to a high of 31.699, then after the midday session slipped, reaching a low of 31.823. The intraday high‑low spread was 0.124 NTD.

Among the major Asian currencies, the Korean won gained about 0.3%, the Thai baht rose roughly 0.1%, the Singapore dollar edged up about 0.05%, the NTD closed up 0.02%, the Japanese yen weakened by nearly 0.2%, and the US dollar index fell about 0.2%.

Yuanta Securities Research noted that persistently high US Treasury yields, volatile US‑Iran geopolitical tensions, and the upcoming US mid‑term elections could heighten global equity market volatility, and advised investors to watch out for the risk of chasing strong‑stock price rallies.

Unified Securities Research said that despite high international oil prices and US Treasury yields, Nvidia’s market cap hit new highs, shifting market focus to tech earnings. Taiwan’s market remains technically strong, with the Taiwan index futures pushing toward the 50,000 mark in the night session, showing bullish confidence. This week, listed companies will release September revenues, and the AI supply‑chain sector is expected to continue delivering solid results. Meanwhile, the World AI Summit and earnings calls for Largan Precision (3008‑TW) and TSMC (2330‑TW) are imminent, providing abundant themes for the Taiwan market.

美國9月就業增長放緩超過預期，前兩個月的非農業就業數據則被大幅下修，幾乎抹去美國聯邦準備理事會(FED)本月再加息的可能性，但地緣政治和油價高企，導致全球債券市場遭拋售，而且美國公債收益率處於數十年高位引發避險資金湧入美元，並據週一標準普爾(S&P)全球調查日本9月服務業採購經理人指數(PMI)終值降至51.3及綜合PMI創5月以來最低52.3，突顯服務業擴張減弱、商業活動與新訂單增長放緩及地震抑制需求，但日本央行(BOJ)副總裁內田真一稱，全球人工智能(AI)可能通過刺激需求和推高資產價格，對經濟產生正面衝擊，而且日本首相高市早苗承諾控制債券發行及迅速採取措施應對市場動盪，安撫擔憂日本財政狀況惡化的投資者，提供日圓支撐，美元兌日圓下滑至157.41低點。
據數據顯示美國9月就業趨勢指數降至107.56，但S&P全球美國9月服務業與綜合PMI終值分別升至58.4及58.8，而且供應管理協會(ISM)公布美國9月非製造業PMI降至54.9，但強投入價格指數創四年多最高74.0，通貨膨脹恐持續高企至明年，推升美元兌日圓至158.29高點。預估今日美元兌日圓支撐於157.50-70，阻力於158.40-60。
◆EUR/USD

昨日S&P全球調查澳洲9月服務業與綜合PMI終值分別升至51.9及51.3，但美國商品期貨交易委員會(CFTC)數據顯示截至9月29日當周，澳幣淨空倉增加，令澳幣承壓；此外，市場擔憂法國能否控制預算赤字及其政治不確定性加劇，加上債券市場劇烈拋售，擔心歐元區主權債務危機重現，並據歐洲央行(ECB)首席經濟學家連恩表示，能源價格飆升拖累經濟增長，可能限制ECB採取緊縮政策力度，打擊歐元兌美元自1.1261高點下挫。

隨著中東原油出口增加及七國集團(G7)釋放石由儲備緩解伊朗戰爭進一步破壞能源供應的擔憂，導致油價回落，並據S&P全球調查9月服務業PMI，法國為去年12月以來首次擴張達51.2，德國則持穩52.9，而且歐元區終值升至十個月新高53.0，但德國機械設備製造業聯合會(VDMA)稱，德國機械與設備製造業連續兩個月增長後，8月訂單按實際值計算較上年同期降5%，而且歐元區10月Sentix投資人信心指數驟降至2.7，重創歐元兌美元至十七個月新低1.1160。預估今日歐元兌美元阻力於1.1215-35，支撐於1.1130-50。
◆GBP/USD

美國通貨膨脹高於目標及經濟強勁，FED於12升息的可能性仍存，甚至未來數月進一步加息，而且美國公債收益率徘徊多年高位附近支撐美元，週一推動英鎊兌美元自1.3250高點下跌。隨後調查顯示S&P全球英國9月服務業與綜合PMI終值分別創6月以來最低達52.1及52.0，縱使企業收取價格指數為5月以來最高，可能加劇英國央行(BOE)擔憂通貨膨脹回升，但法國債務問題打壓歐元，而且市場關注10月28日英國預算案，拖累英鎊兌美元跌至1.3186低點。預估今日英鎊兌美元阻力於1.3220-40，支撐於1.3120-40。

U.S. September job growth slowed more than expected, and the non‑farm payroll figures for the prior two months were sharply revised down, almost eliminating the Federal Reserve’s chance of another rate hike this month. However, geopolitical tensions and high oil prices triggered a sell‑off in global bond markets, and U.S. Treasury yields remain at multi‑decade highs, drawing safe‑haven flows into the dollar. According to Monday’s S&P Global survey, Japan’s September services PMI final reading fell to 51.3 and the composite PMI dropped to a May‑low of 52.3, highlighting weaker service‑sector expansion, slower business activity and new orders, and demand suppression from the earthquake. Yet BOJ Deputy Governor Shinichi Uchida said that global AI could boost demand and lift asset prices, positively impacting the economy, and Prime Minister Kishida promised to curb bond issuance and act swiftly to calm market turbulence, reassuring investors worried about Japan’s fiscal health and providing yen support, pushing USD/JPY down to a low of 157.41.

Data show the U.S. September Employment Trend Index fell to 107.56, but S&P Global’s September U.S. services and composite PMI final readings rose to 58.4 and 58.8 respectively. Meanwhile, the ISM reported the U.S. September non‑manufacturing PMI slipped to 54.9, yet the strong input‑price index hit a four‑year high of 74.0, suggesting inflation could stay elevated into next year and lifting USD/JPY to a high of 158.29. The dollar‑yen pair is expected to find support around 157.50‑70 today, with resistance at 158.40‑60.
EUR/USD

Yesterday S&P Global’s survey showed Australia’s September services and composite PMI final readings rose to 51.9 and 51.3 respectively, but CFTC data indicated that net short positions on the Aussie increased as of the week ending September 29, putting pressure on the AUD. In addition, markets are worried about France’s ability to control its budget deficit and heightened political uncertainty, coupled with a sharp bond‑market sell‑off that revives fears of a sovereign‑debt crisis in the euro area. ECB chief economist Leigh said soaring energy prices are dragging on growth and may limit the ECB’s ability to tighten policy, pushing the euro‑dollar down from its 1.1261 peak.

As Middle‑East oil exports rise and the G7 releases strategic petroleum reserves, concerns that the Iran war could further disrupt supply have eased, sending oil prices lower. According to S&P Global’s September services PMI, France recorded its first expansion since December last year at 51.2, while Germany held steady at 52.9, and the euro‑area composite rose to a ten‑month high of 53.0. However, Germany’s VDMA noted that after two months of growth in machinery and equipment manufacturing, August orders fell 5% year‑on‑year on a real‑terms basis, and the euro‑area Sentix investor confidence index plunged to 2.7 in October, driving the euro‑dollar to a seventeen‑month low of 1.1160. The pair is expected to face resistance around 1.1215‑35 today, with support at 1.1130‑50.
GBP/USD

U.S. inflation remains above target and the economy is strong, leaving the Fed’s chance of a 12‑basis‑point rate hike still alive and even the possibility of further hikes in the coming months. Treasury yields hovering near multi‑year highs continue to support the dollar, pushing the pound‑dollar down from a 1.3250 peak on Monday. Subsequent surveys showed S&P Global’s UK September services and composite PMI final readings fell to June‑low levels of 52.1 and 52.0, even as the corporate‑price‑index hit its highest since May, potentially heightening the Bank of England’s inflation concerns. Meanwhile, France’s debt woes are weighing on the euro, and market focus on the UK budget slated for October 28 is dragging the GBP/USD to a low of 1.3186. The pair is expected to encounter resistance around 1.3220‑40 today, with support at 1.3120‑40.

items.title: 股匯雙漲！巴西總統大選波索納洛領先 股市飆9%創六年高、里亞爾狂升5％  三倍做多ETN暴漲37％
items.title_en: Stocks and Currency Surge! Bolsonaro Leads Brazil Presidential Election, Stock Market Jumps 9% to Six‑Year High, Real Rises 5%, 3× Leveraged ETN Soars 37%
paras: 由於參議員波索納洛在巴西大選首輪投票中意外領先現任總統魯拉，巴西資產大漲，雷亞爾一度飆升5%，股市創六年來最大單日漲幅，三倍做多巴西ETN更大漲37%。
當地時間周日(4日)晚上，巴西總統大選首輪投票結果出爐，前總統之子、自由黨候選人弗拉維奧·波索納洛以約47%得票率意外領先現任總統魯拉以約45%位居第二，兩人將於10月25日進行第二輪角逐。
波索納洛比魯拉更親市場，首輪表現好於預期，帶動巴西股市、匯市全線大漲，巴西基準股指Bovespa一度大漲超9%，創2022年以來最大漲幅，巴西雷亞爾狂升值逾5%。

On Sunday night local time (the 4th), the first‑round results of Brazil's presidential election were released: former president’s son and Liberal Party candidate Flávio Bolsonaro captured about 47% of the vote, unexpectedly ahead of incumbent President Lula who came second with roughly 45%, and the two will face off in a runoff on October 25.

Bolsonaro is seen as more market‑friendly than Lula, and his better‑than‑expected first‑round performance drove a broad rally in Brazil’s equities and foreign‑exchange markets. The benchmark Bovespa index surged more than 9% at one point, the biggest jump since 2022, while the Brazilian real appreciated by over 5%.

Citigroup recommends investors increase exposure to Brazilian equities and local‑currency bonds. In its latest research note, the bank’s strategists wrote: “Bolsonaro is a candidate more favorable to markets, pledging fiscal tightening, privatizations, deregulation and a cut to the value‑added tax; his party’s strong showing in the Senate should help push his legislative agenda through.”

Market pricing forecasts also show a high probability that Bolsonaro will win the October 25 runoff. Citigroup advises buying Brazilian stocks and government bonds maturing in 2031, the so‑called NTN‑F.
